newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends firm after choppy Iraq-led session.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends firm after choppy Iraq-led session.

text.p: IPE Brent crude ended narrowly firmer Tuesday after rocketing early on news of U.S. military action against Iraq and then falling equally sharply on profit-taking, brokers said.
Brent recovered from midafternoon lows as dealers focused on the suspension of the Iraqi oil-for-food agreement and concerns about a possible escalation of the conflict.

"The deal is off and the big worry is about others getting involved. That's when it would get complicated," said a broker. Oct Brent swung between $20.85 and $21.57 a barrel before ending at $22.20, up 21 cents and right in mid-range.

Dealers said an improved technical picture -- the sharp retracement more than filled a chart gap left by Monday's $1.21 rally on Brent -- also encouraged industry and independent floor trader buying later in the session.
"Some of the locals who have sold it all day came back in to cover their shorts when WTI (NYMEX) crude went above $23.40," said a broker.
Washington on Tuesday launched missile strikes against air defence targets in southern Iraq in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks against Kurdish groups in the north of the country.

Oil traders had been expecting Baghdad in the next few weeks to make its first oil sale on world markets since the Gulf War but the May 20 oil-for-food deal was suspended Sunday by the U.N. because of fears for the safety of UN aid monitors in Iraq.
U.S. envoy to the United Nations Edward Gnehm said on Tuesday the terms of the oil-for-food pact must now be reopened.
U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said it would be "some time" before Iraqi exports could be considered again.
Earlier, IPE Sept gas oil closed down $3.25 at $204.50. The Oct Brent-gas oil crack eased, closing at $5.08 a barrel from $5.30. -- Mark Thompson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
